p: Beatrix Potter's The Tale of Peter Rabbit was first published in 1902, and more than a century on, the cheeky bunny in the blue jacket is still a bedtime regular. That's the magic here: little ones walk straight into a world they already know from their books, and grown-ups get a wave of nostalgia for free. Keep an eye out for familiar faces from the stories, as Peter's friends like Benjamin Bunny and Jemima Puddle-Duck are part of the Potter universe the books made famous.

To get the most out of it, read one of the stories together the night before. Toddlers love spotting the bits they recognise, and it turns the visit into an adventure rather than just another play area. Bring socks for everyone, as play spaces like this usually need them, and pack a change of clothes for the inevitable spill or damp knees.

Sessions suit a short attention span, so there's no need to plan a whole day around it. Pair it with a run on the sand, a ride on the trams along the Promenade, or a trip up to Blackpool Zoo if you've got a car and a bit more energy. On the wettest days, Sandcastle Waterpark at South Shore is another indoor shout for slightly older kids. Quieter mornings out of the school holidays tend to suit the tiniest explorers best.
